newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada hopes to lay charges soon in Air India bombing.
newsitem.headline: Canada hopes to lay charges soon in Air India bombing.

text.p: Canadian police said on Tuesday they hoped to have enough evidence within a few months to lay charges in the 1985 bombing of an Air India jet that killed 329 people.

"I'm very confident in saying we will be laying charges in that Air India investigation some time in the new year," Royal Canadian Mounted Police Staff Sgt. Doug Henderson told the Canadian Press news agency.
"(By) the early spring or late winter we'll be laying charges," said Henderson, who oversees the investigation.
Henderson refused to identify the suspects but said they were all residents of British Columbia.
No one has yet been charged in the attack on the Boeing 747 which exploded near Ireland on June 23, 1985 on its way to India from Canada via London.
Canadian police believe they know who planted the bomb but have been unable to gather enough evidence to prosecute those responsible.

Investigators suspect the attack was executed by Sikhs seeking a separate homeland in India's Punjab state. The bombing was intended partly to avenge the Indian army's 1984 storming of the Golden Temple, Sikhism's holiest shrine.

Last year Canadian police revealed they had six suspects in the case and offered the biggest reward in their history -- $1 million Canadian ($740,000 U.S.) -- to spur reluctant witnesses to come forward. They broadened the effort last month by announcing cash rewards for information in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia.
Their prime suspect had been Vancouver-based Sikh activist Talwinder Singh Parmar, founder of the separatist Babbar Khalsa sect, but he was killed in a shoot-out with Indian police in 1992.
The bombing was the biggest mass death in Canada's history. Of the 329 people who died, 278 were Canadians, many of whom were travelling to visit family in India.
